newsitem.title: USA: Postmaster General investigated by Justice Dept.
newsitem.headline: Postmaster General investigated by Justice Dept.

text.p: Postmaster General Marvin Runyon Thursday said he is being investigated by the Justice Department for possible conflict of interest in connection with a Post Office vending machine proposal.
Under the proposal discussed last year, the Postal Service would allow Coca-Cola Co to place its vending machines in post offices around the country, a potentially lucrative deal for both parties.

However, the question of conflict interest arose since Runyon, a former Ford Motor Company executive, owned shares in Coca-Cola that he had purchased in 1977 and were held in blind trust between 1989 and 1994.
In the statement issued by his office, Runyon said he had withdrawn from the discussions and had sold the Coca-Cola stock.
"Never during discussions of the alliance with Coca-Cola did Mr. Runyon consider personal gain and was troubled to learn of the appearance of potential conflict." the statement said.
The Washington Post, quoting two postal sources, said the case was taken before a federal grand jury, which heard testimony from postal employees and others.
The Justice Department had no comment.
However, Justice sources said the investigation was being done by its public integrity unit which handles corruption cases involving government officials.
